parts:
Hi all,

I am an absolute beginner to developing web applications with Shiny, so if I ask an elementary question or post in the wrong place, please say so kindly!

I read in a post on StackOverFlow that: "The shiny-server requires a linux machine. You can not install the shiny server on a Mac."

Does this mean I cannot develop interactive web applications on my MacBookPro? (I would like to develop a Web application with the general aim of large scale online data gathering about peoples' physical attributes, such as weight or height measurements.)

Is there any way to download and install Shiny on a Mac v 10.8.5 at all?

Thank you,

messages.author: b949e0841d7e094b
messages.subject: Re: Newbee - Shiny on Mac OS X
parts: You can develop them on your Mac Os and you can host them on the rstudio beta server for shiny and/or once your own server is in place you can add/remove apps. Someone correct me if I'm wrong but my understanding is that you need linux only to set up your own server. But having said that I haven't set up my own server, I'm using the Rstudio beta server.

I have gone through the first three examples: Hello, Text, Reactivity.

> install.packages(shiny)

> runExample("01_hello")

> runExample("02_text")

> runApp("shinyapp")

What am I doing wrong?

messages.author: 5712068fdf482d27
messages.subject: Re: Newbee - Shiny on Mac OS X
parts:
runExamples are special instances of runApp. You dont need to store shinyapp there. Try typing out the FULL path of shinyapp e.g. runApp(full_path_to_shinyapp) then it should work.

So copy the folder shinyapp to your work directory. You can locate your work directory by typing getwd() into the R console.

messages.author: b949e0841d7e094b
messages.subject: Re: Newbee - Shiny on Mac OS X
parts:
I stick the following at the top of all my scripts that require knowing the current directory, e.g. when saving data or plots, etc..

# set working directory
  if(.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
    setwd("c:/R/shiny")
  } else {
    setwd("~/R/shiny")
  }

I have used the above on Windows, Mac OSX and Ubuntu. Naturally, adapt the directory structure to yours.

You may want to read about the .Renviron (aka Renviron.site) and about the rsession.conf, which store your default settings.

I use the following (add/remove the # depending on platform):

# Windows .Renviron
# RSTUDIO_PDFLATEX = "C:/texlive/2013/bin/win32"
# R_LIBS_USER = "C:/R/library"
# R_USER = "C:/R"
# R_DOC_DIR = "C:/R"
# HOME = "C:"
 
# Linux Renviron.site
# R_LIBS_USER = "~/R/library"
# R_USER = "~/R"
# R_DOC_DIR = "~/R"
# HOME = "/home/patrick" # not needed

# MacOSX Renviron.site
 R_LIBS_USER = "~/R/library"
 R_USER = "~/R"
 R_DOC_DIR = "~/R"
# HOME = "/Users/PatrickToche" # not needed

# If there are multiple versions of the same package,
# the local library is searched first:
 R_LIBS_SITE=${R_LIBS_SITE-'/usr/local/lib/R/site-library:/usr/lib/R/site-library:/usr/lib/R/library'}

# By default RStudio sets the R_LIBS_USER environment variable to ~/R/library.
